titlePlain: Pods, ReplicaSets, and Deployments: the Real
subtitle: Lesson 10 · Kubernetes Architecture & Core Objects

code:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: web-app
  labels:
    app: web-app
spec:
  containers:
    - name: web-app
      image: myregistry.azurecr.io/web-app:1.4.2
      ports:
        - containerPort: 8080
caption: One Pod, no self-healing — if its node dies, nothing brings it back.

steps.label: Pod
steps.sub: the smallest deployable unit — containers scheduled together

steps.label: ReplicaSet
steps.sub: reconciles COUNT — keeps N Pods matching a label selector alive

steps.label: Deployment
steps.sub: reconciles CHANGE — creates a new ReplicaSet per template update

code:
kubectl apply -f replicaset.yaml
kubectl get pods -l app=web-app
kubectl delete pod web-app-rs-k2j9m
kubectl get pods -l app=web-app

# a replacement Pod appears within seconds —
# the ReplicaSet only noticed the COUNT dropped from 3 to 2
caption: A ReplicaSet never edits a running Pod; it only creates or deletes whole Pods to match the count.

code:
kubectl get deployments
NAME       READY   UP-TO-DATE   AVAILABLE
web-app    3/3     3            3

kubectl get replicasets
NAME                   DESIRED   CURRENT   READY
web-app-7d9f8c6b5d     3         3         3

kubectl get pods
web-app-7d9f8c6b5d-x2k9p   1/1   Running
web-app-7d9f8c6b5d-j4m2q   1/1   Running
caption: Deployment -> ReplicaSet -> Pod, visible directly in the names kubectl prints.
